notMeasured.reason: A write measured with COMMIT mutates the corpus and makes the run non-repeatable; measured with ROLLBACK it omits the WAL flush, which is the dominant cost. Neither is worth a baseline.
As Task create, plus optimistic-concurrency retry cost that does not exist until the command layer does.
A transition is a command with guard evaluation, dependency checks, and four writes in one transaction (docs/23). Its SQL alone would understate it by more than it measures.
There is no cache. The docs/30 target is a property of the epoch-keyed cache in docs/04, which is Phase 1 code.
No API process exists. Every number here is a database round trip and excludes everything the server does around it.
Cases run single-threaded, one query in flight. Contention, pool saturation, and the read/write mix in docs/30 §Throughput are not exercised.

baseline.justification: Reference-tooling baseline for the m4-10c-16gb environment (F-007). Corpus is tools/casual-task-seed --scale small (50,000 tasks), generated after the one-level comment-threading fix, loaded into a clean PostgreSQL 16 and ANALYZEd. Measured as taskforge_app with RLS applied. RE-MEASURED after the list_page_cursor fixture was fixed: the cursor used to be the newest row, so the case measured the head of the index it claimed to be avoiding; it now sits 500 rows deep and pays a real keyset descent. Every case is inside its docs/30 p95 target at this scale. NOT a gating baseline, and it cannot become one by accident: docs/30 names an 8 vCPU / 32 GB reference machine, this is a laptop, and the harness refuses to compare across environments. Run-to-run variance on this machine is material — roundtrip_floor p95 moved 56->78 us between two idle runs, roughly 40% — which is itself the argument for docs/30's dedicated reference machine. Treat these as shape, not precision. full_text_search is the number NOT to extrapolate: D-043 shows its plan degrades to a sequential scan under RLS at reference scale.
